name: Qwen3.8-27B
purpose: Qwen states a compact, deployment-friendly dense model for coding, professional work, research and long-horizon agentic tasks, with greater reliability on multi-step tasks; for developers who self-host or plug it into existing tooling.

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: LICENSE read: Apache License 2.0 full text. The sibling Qwen3.8-Flash-Next uses the Qwen Community License instead. LICENSE file in the repo read: Apache License 2.0 with the vendor copyright appendix ('Copyright 2026 Alibaba Cloud'), no additional terms. Same md5 as the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and 9B LICENSE files.

architecture.kind: dense hybrid Gated DeltaNet + gated attention with vision encoder
architecture.attention: 16 x (3 Gated DeltaNet + 1 gated attention); 24 Q / 4 KV heads, head dim 256
architecture.drafter: MTP trained (multi-step); a DFlash2 drafter exists (research/08-models.md)
architecture.why_this_design: The card pitches coding and agents first and a native vision-language dense model; reasons for the dense layout are not stated in the text we read. Check: the Qwen3.8 blog. Card: built on the Qwen3.5 architectural foundation (hybrid Gated DeltaNet and gated attention); Qwen3.8-27B 'brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model'. Qwen3.5 card: 'Efficient Hybrid Architecture: Gated Delta Networks combined with sparse Mixture-of-Experts deliver high-throughput inference with minimal latency and cost overhead.'

strengths: Almost level with Flash-Next on SWE-bench Pro (61.7 vs 62.5, vendor)
Fits entirely in 16 GB VRAM as IQ3 (10.1 GB)
Strongest knowledge and reasoning numbers of the models that fit 16 GB at 3-bit (vendor GPQA 89.2)
Vision and video input in the same checkpoint
weaknesses: Full attention KV at 256K does not fit VRAM next to the weights (about 36K tokens fp16 with IQ3 on 16 GB, estimate)
About 4x the prefill cost per token of Flash-Next (research/08 estimate)
Thinking on by default; lower reasoning effort does not always cut task time (card)
Overthinks by default (effort xhigh); time to first answer token 128 s at xhigh in the Artificial Analysis run
AA-Omniscience is negative at every effort level: more wrong answers than correct ones
Dense: one user found it 7 to 8x slower than the 35B-A3B MoE
soft.behavior: Thinking on by default, reasoning_effort xhigh; medium, low and enable_thinking=false are available. Vendor sampling T=1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 (thinking). The card warns that lower effort can raise latency in multi-turn agent tasks.
best_for: fully-in-VRAM coding agent on 16 to 24 GB cards with moderate context
Hard reasoning and research synthesis where latency is acceptable
Long documents up to roughly 64-75K tokens on 16 GB (KV bound, research/08)
avoid_for: Factual look-ups without a search tool
soft.maturity: Qwen: very large community (1,873 quantizations listed on the card), fast release cadence.

user_reports.summary: Simon Willison: excellent but overthinks by default; one SVG test took 21 minutes and 22,276 reasoning tokens at the default setting.

Infinite tool-call loops with thinking switched off on some questions; a reply says it becomes weak on complex coding or debugging tasks and loops on tool calls, simple tasks are fine. Deployment details not given.

Independent C++/CUDA engine converted it to NVFP4 (15 GB, 14.1 GiB resident on one RTX 5090): greedy decoding byte-identical across runs and reloads, native XML tool-call format parses without heuristics, tokenizer reproduced exactly.

tona_fit.reason: Strongest independent coding evidence of the 16 GB class: Coding Index 68.1 (mirror of the Artificial Analysis index) against 41.9 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Apache-2.0 text verified, vendor LiveCodeBench v6 90.3, fits 12 to 16 GB VRAM at 10 to 17 GB (UD-Q4_K_M 16.6 GB). Offered for the 12 and 16 GB classes as the dense option; long default thinking is a usage caveat. Best dense generalist for 16-24 GB by independent evidence too: PeerBench German Elo 1634 (INCLUDE DE 87.9, MuSR DE 86.1, MMLU-ProX DE 79.9), highest Elo among the 27-31B open models listed (Qwen3.6 27B 1615, Gemma 4 31B 1477), plus Apache-2.0 (text read) and the vendor numbers. Costs: long default thinking (reasoning_effort default xhigh) and tool-loop reports with thinking off. Missing dense module in Tona is only a blocker.
blockers: Tona has no dense Qwen3.8 module yet (engine support, not quality)
default thinking length hurts chat latency
dense decode on 16 GB is slower per token than the A3B MoEs (bandwidth bound, estimate)
no dense qwen3_5 module in Tona
tool-call loops reported with thinking off
